title: Reverse Alternate K Groups
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list and a positive integer `k`, process the list in consecutive groups of `k` nodes starting from the head: **reverse** the first group, leave the second group **unchanged**, reverse the third, leave the fourth unchanged, and so on.

If the list ends in the middle of a group, that partial group follows the same rule as a full one: it is reversed if it falls on a reversing turn and left as-is otherwise. Return the head of the modified list. Only links may change, not node values.

**Example 1:**
```
Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9], k = 3
Output: [3,2,1,4,5,6,9,8,7]
Explanation: Group [1,2,3] is reversed, [4,5,6] is kept, and [7,8,9] is reversed.
```

**Example 2:**
```
Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7], k = 2
Output: [2,1,3,4,6,5,7]
Explanation: Reverse [1,2], keep [3,4], reverse [5,6], keep the partial group [7].
```

**Example 3:**
```
Input: head = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8], k = 3
Output: [3,2,1,4,5,6,8,7]
Explanation: Reverse [1,2,3], keep [4,5,6], and the partial group [7,8] falls on a reversing turn, so it becomes [8,7].
```

solution_approach: Brute force: copy the node values into an array, reverse every alternate slice of length k (including a trailing partial slice on a reversing turn), and write the values back, which is O(n) time but O(n) extra space and modifies values instead of links. Optimal: use a dummy node and a tail pointer to the end of the processed part. On a reversing turn, reverse up to k nodes in place with the three-pointer technique, attach the reversed block after tail, and move tail to the block's last node (the group's original first node). On a keeping turn, simply advance tail up to k nodes. Alternate until the list ends. Every node is visited a constant number of times, giving O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
hints: Treat the list as a sequence of alternating 'reverse' and 'skip' phases, each covering up to k nodes.

Reversing up to k nodes in place is the same as the standard reversal, just stopping after k steps or at the end of the list; keep track of the node before the group and the group's original first node.

Use a dummy head and a tail pointer: on a reverse turn, reverse up to k nodes and link them after tail, then set tail to the group's original first node; on a skip turn, advance tail k nodes (or to the end).
